# GROMACS - A Molecular Dynamics Package

GROMACS is a versatile package to perform molecular dynamics, i.e., simulate
the Newtonian equations of motion for systems with hundreds to millions of
particles.

## What GROMACS Does

GROMACS is primarily designed for biochemical molecules like proteins, lipids,
and nucleic acids that have a lot of complicated bonded interactions. However,
since GROMACS is extremely fast at calculating the nonbonded interactions
(that usually dominate simulations) many groups are also using it for research
on non-biological systems, e.g., polymers and fluid dynamics.

## Usage

GROMACS includes many tools for preparing, running and analyzing molecular
dynamics simulations. These are all structured as part of a single `gmx`
wrapper binary, invoked with commands like:

    gmx grompp    # Prepare a simulation
    gmx mdrun     # Run a simulation
    gmx help      # Show available commands

If you have installed an MPI version of GROMACS, by default the gmx binary
is called `gmx_mpi` and you should adapt accordingly.

### Basic Workflow

A typical simulation workflow involves:

1. **System Preparation**: Start with a structure file (e.g., PDB format)
2. **Topology Generation**: Generate molecular topology with `gmx pdb2gmx`
3. **Simulation Setup**: Prepare the simulation with `gmx grompp`
4. **Run Simulation**: Execute the dynamics with `gmx mdrun`
5. **Analysis**: Analyze results with various analysis tools

### Key File Types

- `.pdb` - Protein Data Bank structure files
- `.top` - Molecular topology files (complete description of interactions)
- `.gro` - GROMACS coordinate files
- `.xtc`, `.trr` - Trajectory files (simulation output)
- `.mdp` - Molecular dynamics parameter files (simulation settings)
- `.tpr` - Portable binary run input file

### Command-Line Interface

All GROMACS commands require an option before any arguments. Options start
with a single dash (or double dash). For example:

    gmx mdrun -s topol.tpr -v
    gmx grompp -f input.mdp -c conf.gro -p topol.top -o output.tpr

Use `gmx help <command>` or `gmx <command> -h` for detailed help on any tool.

## Features

GROMACS provides:

- **Molecular Dynamics Simulations**: Simulate the time evolution of molecular systems
- **Energy Minimization**: Find stable configurations of molecular systems
- **Free Energy Calculations**: Compute thermodynamic properties
- **Analysis Tools**: Extensive toolkit for trajectory analysis
- **Multiple Force Fields**: Support for various molecular force fields
- **Parallel Computing**: Support for efficient parallel execution

## Resources

- Online documentation: http://manual.gromacs.org/
- Forums: http://forums.gromacs.org/
- Tutorials: http://tutorials.gromacs.org/
- Issue tracking: https://gitlab.com/gromacs/gromacs/-/issues

## Citation

If you use GROMACS for research, please cite the appropriate papers. See the
CITATION.cff file for complete citation metadata, or visit:
https://www.gromacs.org/articles.html

Key publications include:

- GROMACS: A message-passing parallel molecular dynamics implementation
  H.J.C. Berendsen, D. van der Spoel and R. van Drunen
  Comp. Phys. Comm. 91, 43-56 (1995)
  DOI: https://doi.org/10.1016/0010-4655(95)00042-E

- GROMACS 4: Algorithms for highly efficient, load-balanced, and scalable
  molecular simulation
  B. Hess and C. Kutzner and D. van der Spoel and E. Lindahl
  J. Chem. Theory Comput. 4 (2008) pp. 435-447
  DOI: https://doi.org/10.1021/ct700301q

- GROMACS: High performance molecular simulations through multi-level
  parallelism from laptops to supercomputers
  M. J. Abraham, T. Murtola, R. Schulz, S. Páll, J. C. Smith, B. Hess,
  E. Lindahl, SoftwareX, 1, (2015), 19-25
  DOI: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.softx.2015.06.001

## License

GROMACS is free software, distributed under the GNU Lesser General Public
License (LGPL), version 2.1. See the COPYING file for full license text.

Option -c checks for presence of coordinates, velocities and box in the file,
for close contacts (smaller than -vdwfac and not bonded, i.e. not between
-bonlo and -bonhi, all relative to the sum of both Van der Waals radii) and

If an index file, is given its contents will be summarized.

If both a trajectory and a .tpr file are given (with -s1) the program will
check whether the bond lengths defined in the tpr file are indeed correct in
the trajectory. If not you may have non-matching files due to e.g. deshuffling
or due to problems with virtual sites. With these flags, gmx check provides a
quick check for such problems.

The program can compare two run input (.tpr) files when both -s1 and -s2 are
supplied. When comparing run input files this way, the default relative
tolerance is reduced to 0.000001 and the absolute tolerance set to zero to
find any differences not due to minor compiler optimization differences,
although you can of course still set any other tolerances through the options.

DESCRIPTION

Index groups are necessary for almost every GROMACS program. All these
programs can generate default index groups. You ONLY have to use gmx make_ndx
when you need SPECIAL index groups. There is a default index group for the
whole system, 9 default index groups for proteins, and a default index group
is generated for every other residue name.

When no index file is supplied, also gmx make_ndx will generate the default
groups. With the index editor you can select on atom, residue and chain names
and numbers. When a run input file is supplied you can also select on atom
type. You can use boolean operations, you can split groups into chains,
residues or atoms. You can delete and rename groups. Type 'h' in the editor
for more details.

The atom numbering in the editor and the index file starts at 1.

The -twin switch duplicates all index groups with an offset of -natoms, which
is useful for Computational Electrophysiology double-layer membrane setups.

index groups.  It covers nearly all of gmx make_ndx functionality, and in many
cases much more.

SYNOPSIS

            [-o [<.gro/.g96/...>]] [-nbox <vector>] [-dist <vector>]
            [-seed <int>] [-[no]rot] [-maxrot <vector>] [-[no]renumber]

DESCRIPTION

gmx genconf multiplies a given coordinate file by simply stacking them on top
of each other, like a small child playing with wooden blocks. The program
makes a grid of user-defined proportions (-nbox), and interspaces the grid
point with an extra space -dist.

When option -rot is used the program does not check for overlap between
molecules on grid points. It is recommended to make the box in the input file
at least as big as the coordinates + van der Waals radius.

If the optional trajectory file is given, conformations are not generated, but

import subprocess,os,pathlib,json
ROOT=pathlib.Path('/workspace'); EX=str(ROOT/'executable')
env=dict(os.environ,GMX_NO_QUOTES='1',GMX_MAXBACKUP='-1')
def run(name,args,inp='',cwd=None,quiet=True):
 d=ROOT/'observations'/name; d.mkdir(exist_ok=True,parents=True)
 p=subprocess.run([EX]+(['-quiet'] if quiet else [])+args,input=inp.encode(),capture_output=True,cwd=cwd or d,env=env,timeout=8)
 (d/'stdout').write_bytes(p.stdout); (d/'stderr').write_bytes(p.stderr);(d/'call.json').write_text(json.dumps([args,inp,p.returncode]))
 print('\n###',name,args,'=>',p.returncode);print(p.stdout.decode(errors='replace'),end='');print(p.stderr.decode(errors='replace'),end='')
 return p
if __name__=='__main__':
 cases=[('badhelp',['help','nonsense']),('double',['--quiet','-h']),('common_unknown',['-foo']),('common_bool',['-quiet','false','-h']),('common_int',['-nice','a']),('help_version',['editconf','-version']),('tool_help',['editconf','-h','-bad']),('tool_bad',['editconf','-bad']),('tool_long',['editconf','--help']),('tool_pos',['editconf','file.gro']),('missing_file',['editconf','-f','x.gro']),('missing_ext',['editconf','-f','x']),('bad_ext',['editconf','-f','x.xyz']),('bad_enum',['editconf','-bt','x']),('bad_real',['editconf','-d','abc']),('bad_vec',['editconf','-box','1','2']),('bad_bool',['editconf','-c','false']),('sel_default',['select']),('grompp_default',['grompp']),('mdrun_default',['mdrun']),('dump_default',['dump']),('pdb2gmx_default',['pdb2gmx'])]
 for name,args in cases:
  try:run(name,args)
  except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:print(name,'TIMEOUT')
PY
python3 observations/probe.py > observations/validation.txt
sed -n '1,220p' observations/validation.txt

### tool_help ['editconf', '-h', '-bad'] => 0
SYNOPSIS

gmx editconf [-f [<.gro/.g96/...>]] [-n [<.ndx>]] [-bf [<.dat>]]
             [-o [<.gro/.g96/...>]] [-mead [<.pqr>]] [-[no]w] [-[no]ndef]
             [-bt <enum>] [-box <vector>] [-angles <vector>] [-d <real>]
             [-[no]c] [-center <vector>] [-aligncenter <vector>]
             [-align <vector>] [-translate <vector>] [-rotate <vector>]
             [-[no]princ] [-scale <vector>] [-density <real>] [-[no]pbc]
             [-resnr <int>] [-[no]grasp] [-rvdw <real>] [-[no]sig56]
             [-[no]vdwread] [-[no]atom] [-[no]legend] [-label <string>]
             [-[no]conect]

DESCRIPTION

gmx editconf converts generic structure format to .gro, .g96 or .pdb.

The box can be modified with options -box, -d and -angles. Both -box and -d
will center the system in the box, unless -noc is used. The -center option can
be used to shift the geometric center of the system from the default of (x/2,
y/2, z/2) implied by -c to some other value.

Option -bt determines the box type: triclinic is a triclinic box, cubic is a
rectangular box with all sides equal dodecahedron represents a rhombic
dodecahedron and octahedron is a truncated octahedron. The last two are
special cases of a triclinic box. The length of the three box vectors of the
truncated octahedron is the shortest distance between two opposite hexagons.
Relative to a cubic box with some periodic image distance, the volume of a
dodecahedron with this same periodic distance is 0.71 times that of the cube,
and that of a truncated octahedron is 0.77 times.

Option -box requires only one value for a cubic, rhombic dodecahedral, or
truncated octahedral box.

With -d and a triclinic box the size of the system in the x-, y-, and
z-directions is used. With -d and cubic, dodecahedron or octahedron boxes, the
dimensions are set to the diameter of the system (largest distance between
atoms) plus twice the specified distance.

Option -angles is only meaningful with option -box and a triclinic box and
cannot be used with option -d.

When -n or -ndef is set, a group can be selected for calculating the size and
the geometric center, otherwise the whole system is used.

-rotate rotates the coordinates and velocities.

-princ aligns the principal axes of the system along the coordinate axes, with
the longest axis aligned with the x-axis. This may allow you to decrease the
box volume, but beware that molecules can rotate significantly in a
nanosecond.

Scaling is applied before any of the other operations are performed. Boxes and
coordinates can be scaled to give a certain density (option -density). Note
that this may be inaccurate in case a .gro file is given as input. A special
feature of the scaling option is that when the factor -1 is given in one
dimension, one obtains a mirror image, mirrored in one of the planes. When one
uses -1 in three dimensions, a point-mirror image is obtained.

Groups are selected after all operations have been applied.

Periodicity can be removed in a crude manner. It is important that the box
vectors at the bottom of your input file are correct when the periodicity is
to be removed.

When writing .pdb files, B-factors can be added with the -bf option. B-factors
are read from a file with with following format: first line states number of
entries in the file, next lines state an index followed by a B-factor. The
B-factors will be attached per residue unless the number of B-factors is
larger than the number of the residues or unless the -atom option is set.
Obviously, any type of numeric data can be added instead of B-factors. -legend
will produce a row of CA atoms with B-factors ranging from the minimum to the
maximum value found, effectively making a legend for viewing.

With the option -mead a special .pdb (.pqr) file for the MEAD electrostatics
program (Poisson-Boltzmann solver) can be made. A further prerequisite is that
the input file is a run input file. The B-factor field is then filled with the
Van der Waals radius of the atoms while the occupancy field will hold the
charge.

The option -grasp is similar, but it puts the charges in the B-factor and the
radius in the occupancy.

Option -align allows alignment of the principal axis of a specified group
against the given vector, with an optional center of rotation specified by
-aligncenter.

Finally, with option -label, editconf can add a chain identifier to a .pdb
file, which can be useful for analysis with e.g. Rasmol.

To convert a truncated octrahedron file produced by a package which uses a
cubic box with the corners cut off (such as GROMOS), use:

  gmx editconf -f in -rotate 0 45 35.264 -bt o -box veclen -o out

where veclen is the size of the cubic box times sqrt(3)/2.

OPTIONS

Options to specify input files:

 -f      [<.gro/.g96/...>]  (conf.gro)
           Structure file: gro g96 pdb brk ent esp tpr
 -n      [<.ndx>]           (index.ndx)      (Opt.)
           Index file
 -bf     [<.dat>]           (bfact.dat)      (Opt.)
           Generic data file

Options to specify output files:

 -o      [<.gro/.g96/...>]  (out.gro)        (Opt.)
           Structure file: gro g96 pdb brk ent esp
 -mead   [<.pqr>]           (mead.pqr)       (Opt.)
           Coordinate file for MEAD

</output>

"""Numerical utilities for tabular data and model interaction potentials."""
import os,math,re
from common import *
STATS_HEADER='                                      std. dev.    relative deviation of\n                       standard       ---------   cumulants from those of\nset      average       deviation      sqrt(n-1)   a Gaussian distribition\n                                                      cum. 3   cum. 4'

def read_data(app,path):
    o=app.opts;blocks=[[]];ncols=None;linecount=0
    for raw in open(path,errors='replace'):
        line=raw.strip()
        if not line or line.startswith(('#','@')):continue
        if line.startswith('&'):
            if o.get('n',1)>len(blocks):blocks.append([]);ncols=None;continue
            break
        vals=[]
        for t in line.split():
            try:vals.append(float(t))
            except ValueError:break
        if not vals:continue
        has_time=o.get('time',True)
        if ncols is None:ncols=len(vals)
        if len(vals)<ncols:
            app.err('Invalid line in %s:\n%s\nUsing zeros for the last %d sets'%(path,raw.rstrip('\n'),ncols-len(vals)))
            vals += [0.]*(ncols-len(vals))
        if not has_time:vals=[float(linecount)]+vals
        if len(vals)==1:vals=[float(linecount),vals[0]]
        linecount+=1
        if o.get('b',-1)>=0 and vals[0]<o['b']:continue
        if o.get('e',-1)>=0 and vals[0]>o['e']:continue
        blocks[-1].append(vals)
    if not blocks[0]:return [],[]
    if o.get('n',1)>1:
        count=min(len(x) for x in blocks);times=[row[0] for row in blocks[0][:count]]
        datasets=[[row[1] for row in block[:count]] for block in blocks]
    else:
        times=[row[0] for row in blocks[0]];ncols=len(blocks[0][0]);datasets=[[row[j] if j<len(row) else 0 for row in blocks[0]] for j in range(1,ncols)]
    return times,datasets

def analyze(app):
    o=app.opts;p=app.present;t,sets=read_data(app,o['f']);n=len(t);ns=len(sets)
    dt=(t[-1]-t[0])/(n-1) if n>1 else 1.
    app.out('Read %d sets of %d points, dt = %s\n'%(ns,n,g(dt)))
    if not n:return
    if o['d']:
        app.out('Calculating the derivative as (f[i+1]-f[i])/(1*dt)\n')
        sets=[[div(y[j+1]-y[j],dt) for j in range(n-1)] for y in sets];n-=1;t=t[:n]
    if o['integrate']:
        app.out('Calculating the integral using the trapezium rule')
        for i,y in enumerate(sets[:1] if o['xydy'] else sets,1):
            sums=[0.]
            for j in range(1,n):sums.append(sums[-1]+.5*(t[j]-t[j-1])*(y[j]+y[j-1]))
            inte=sums[-1]
            if 'aver_start' in p:
                valid=[v for tm,v in zip(t,sums) if tm>=o['aver_start']];inte=sum(valid)/len(valid) if valid else 0
            err=0.
            if o['xydy'] and len(sets)>1:err=math.sqrt(sum(((t[j]-t[j-1])/2)**2*(sets[1][j]**2+sets[1][j-1]**2) for j in range(1,n)))
            app.out('Integral %d  %10.5f  +/- %10.5f'%(i,inte,err))
    means=[];stds=[];app.out(STATS_HEADER)
    for i,y in enumerate(sets,1):
        av=sum(y)/n if n else 0.;d=[v-av for v in y];var=sum(x*x for x in d)/n if n else 0;sd=math.sqrt(max(0,var));sem=sd/math.sqrt(n-1) if n>1 else 0
        third=(sum(x**3 for x in d)/n)/(sd**3)*math.sqrt(math.pi/8) if sd else 0;fourth=(sum(x**4 for x in d)/n)/(3*var*var)-1 if var else 0
        app.out('SS%-2d %13.6e  %13.6e  %13.6e    %8.3f %8.3f'%(i,av,sd,sem,third,fourth));means.append(av);stds.append(sd)
    app.out('')
    if o.get('regression'):
        if ns>1 and not o['xydy']:
            xs=sets[1:];a=least_squares(xs,sets[0]);chi=sum((y-sum(a[j]*xs[j][i] for j in range(len(xs))))**2 for i,y in enumerate(sets[0]))
            app.out('Fitting %d data points in %d sets\nchi2 = %s\nA = %s'%(n,ns-1,g(chi),''.join(' %s'%g(x) for x in a)))
        else:
            y=sets[0];xm=sum(t)/n;ym=sum(y)/n;vx=sum((x-xm)**2 for x in t);vy=sum((x-ym)**2 for x in y);cross=sum((x-xm)*(v-ym) for x,v in zip(t,y));a=div(cross,vx);b=ym-a*xm
            chi=sum((a*x+b-v)**2 for x,v in zip(t,y));cc=div(cross,math.sqrt(vx*vy))
            app.out('Fitting data to a function f(x) = ax + b\nMinimizing residual chi2 = Sum_i w_i [f(x_i) - y_i]2\nError estimates will be given if w_i (sigma) values are given\n(use option -xydy).\n\nChi2                    = %s\nS (Sqrt(Chi2/(n-2))     = %s\nCorrelation coefficient = %.1f%%\n\na    = %s\nb    = %s'%(g(chi*n/(n-2) if n>2 else chi),g(math.sqrt(chi/(n-2))) if n>2 else '-nan',100*cc,g(a),g(b)))
    if 'msd' in p:
        text=app.xvg_header('Mean square displacement','Time (ps)','MSD');count=(n+1)//2
        for y in sets:
            app.err('0')
            for lag in range(count):
                value=sum((y[j+lag]-y[j])**2 for j in range(n-lag))/(n-lag)
                text+=' %s %8s\n'%(g(lag*dt),g(value))
            text+='\n'
        app.write(o['msd'],text)
    if 'cc' in p:
        s=app.xvg_header('Cosine content','Set','Cosine content')
        for i,y in enumerate(sets,1):
            a=sum(v*math.cos(i*math.pi*j/(n-1)) for j,v in enumerate(y)) if n>1 else 0
            cc=div(2*a*a,n*sum(v*v for v in y))
            app.out('Cosine content of set %d with %.1f periods: %s'%(i,.5*i,g(cc)));s+=' %d %s\n'%(i,g(cc))
        app.out('');app.write(o['cc'],s)
    if 'ac' in p:
        count=(n+1)//2 if o['acflen']<0 else min(n,o['acflen']);corr=[]
        for idx,y in enumerate(sets):
            data=[v-means[idx] if o['subav'] else v for v in y]
            c=[sum(data[j+lag]*data[j] for j in range(n-lag))/(n-lag) for lag in range(count)]
            if o['normalize'] and c and c[0]:c=[x/c[0] for x in c]
            corr.append(c)
        if o['oneacf']:corr=[[sum(x)/len(x) for x in zip(*corr)]]
        s=app.xvg_header('Autocorrelation','Time (ps)','C(t)');ct=[]
        for vals in corr:
            for j,v in enumerate(vals):s+='%10.3f %11.5f\n'%(dt*j,v)
            s+='&\n';ct.append(sum((vals[j]+vals[j-1])*dt*.5 for j in range(1,len(vals))))
        app.write(o['ac'],s)
        if count:app.err('%d, time=%s'%(count-1,g((count-1)*dt)))
        av=sum(ct)/len(ct) if ct else 0.;sd=math.sqrt(sum((x-av)**2 for x in ct)/len(ct)) if ct else 0
        app.out('Average correlation time %.3f Std. Dev. %.3f Error %.3f (ps)\n'%(av,sd,sd/math.sqrt(max(1,len(ct)-1))))
    if 'dist' in p:
        bw=o['bw'];low=min(min(y) for y in sets);high=max(max(y) for y in sets)
        start=int(low/bw)-1;bins=int(high/bw)-int(low/bw)+4
        bins=max(1,min(1000000,bins));app.err('Making distributions with %d bins'%bins)
        s=app.xvg_header('Distribution')
        for y in sets:
            hist=[0]*bins
            for v in y:
                pos=int(v/bw+.5)-start
                if 0<=pos<bins:hist[pos]+=1
            for j,h in enumerate(hist):s+=' %s  %s\n'%(g((start+j)*bw),g(h/(n*bw)))
            s+='&\n'
        app.write(o['dist'],s)
    if 'av' in p:
        error=o['errbar'];s='@TYPE xydy\n' if error!='none' else ''
        for j,tm in enumerate(t):
            values=[y[j] for y in sets];av=sum(values)/ns;s+=' %s %s'%(g(tm),g(av))
            if error!='none':
                v=sum((x-av)**2 for x in values)/ns
                if error in ['error','90']:v/=max(1,ns-1)

                if error=='90':sd*=1.644853626951
                s+=' '+g(sd)
            s+='\n'
        app.write(o['av'],s)
    if 'ee' in p:
        app.write(o['ee'],app.xvg_header('Error estimates','Block size (ps)','Error estimate'))

def least_squares(xs,y):
    n=len(xs);a=[[sum(x*v for x,v in zip(xs[i],xs[j])) for j in range(n)]+[sum(x*v for x,v in zip(xs[i],y))] for i in range(n)]
    for k in range(n):
        q=max(range(k,n),key=lambda j:abs(a[j][k]));a[k],a[q]=a[q],a[k]
        if abs(a[k][k])<1e-15:continue
        den=a[k][k];a[k]=[x/den for x in a[k]]
        for j in range(n):
            if j!=k:
                b=a[j][k];a[j]=[x-b*v for x,v in zip(a[j],a[k])]
    return [row[-1] for row in a]

def sigeps(app):
    o=app.opts;p=app.present;n=o['pow'];c6=f32(o['c6']);cn=f32(o['cn']);sigma=0.;eps=0.;A=f32(o['A']);B=f32(o['B']);C=f32(o['C'])
    buck=any(k in p for k in ['A','B','C'])
    if buck:
        rmin=div(n,B);c6=C;cn=f32(c6*power(rmin,n-6)*6/n);sigma=f32(power(div(cn,c6),div(1,n-6)));eps=f32(div(c6,4*power(sigma,6)))
    else:

        elif 'c6' in p or 'cn' in p:

        rmin=f32(power(div(n*cn,6*c6),div(1,n-6))) if sigma else 0
        minimum=div(cn,power(rmin,n))-div(c6,power(rmin,6))
        app.out('c6    = %12.5e, c%d    = %12.5e'%(c6,n,cn))
        app.out('sigma = %12.5f, epsilon = %12.5f'%(sigma,eps))
        app.out('Van der Waals minimum at %s, V = %s\n'%(g(rmin),g(minimum)))
        B=f32(div(n,rmin));C=c6;A=f32(div(cn,power(rmin,n))*math.exp(n))
        app.out('Fit of Lennard Jones (%d-6) to Buckingham:\nA = %s, B = %s, C = %s'%(n,g(A),g(B),g(C)))

    app.write(o['o'],s)

SYNOPSIS

gmx genrestr [-f [<.gro/.g96/...>]] [-n [<.ndx>]] [-o [<.itp>]]
             [-of [<.ndx>]] [-fc <vector>] [-freeze <real>] [-[no]disre]
             [-disre_dist <real>] [-disre_frac <real>] [-disre_up2 <real>]
             [-cutoff <real>] [-[no]constr]

DESCRIPTION

gmx genrestr produces an #include file for a topology containing a list of
atom numbers and three force constants for the x-, y-, and z-direction based
on the contents of the -f file. A single isotropic force constant may be given
on the command line instead of three components.

WARNING: Position restraints are interactions within molecules, therefore they
must be included within the correct [ moleculetype ] block in the topology.
The atom indices within the [ position_restraints ] block must be within the
range of the atom indices for that molecule type. Since the atom numbers in
every moleculetype in the topology start at 1 and the numbers in the input
file for gmx genrestr number consecutively from 1, gmx genrestr will only
produce a useful file for the first molecule. You may wish to edit the
resulting index file to remove the lines for later atoms, or construct a
suitable index group to provide as input to gmx genrestr.

The -of option produces an index file that can be used for freezing atoms. In
this case, the input file must be a .pdb file.

With the -disre option, half a matrix of distance restraints is generated
instead of position restraints. With this matrix, that one typically would
apply to Calpha atoms in a protein, one can maintain the overall conformation
of a protein without tieing it to a specific position (as with position
restraints).

OPTIONS

Options to specify input files:

 -f      [<.gro/.g96/...>]  (conf.gro)
           Structure file: gro g96 pdb brk ent esp tpr
 -n      [<.ndx>]           (index.ndx)      (Opt.)
           Index file

Options to specify output files:

 -o      [<.itp>]           (posre.itp)
           Include file for topology
 -of     [<.ndx>]           (freeze.ndx)     (Opt.)
           Index file

Other options:

 -fc     <vector>           (1000 1000 1000)
           Force constants (kJ/mol nm^2)
 -freeze <real>             (0)
           If the -of option or this one is given an index file will be
           written containing atom numbers of all atoms that have a B-factor
           less than the level given here
 -[no]disre                 (no)
           Generate a distance restraint matrix for all the atoms in index
 -disre_dist <real>         (0.1)
           Distance range around the actual distance for generating distance
           restraints
 -disre_frac <real>         (0)
           Fraction of distance to be used as interval rather than a fixed
           distance. If the fraction of the distance that you specify here is
           less than the distance given in the previous option, that one is
           used instead.
 -disre_up2 <real>          (1)
           Distance between upper bound for distance restraints, and the
           distance at which the force becomes constant (see manual)
 -cutoff <real>             (-1)
           Only generate distance restraints for atoms pairs within cutoff
           (nm)
 -[no]constr                (no)
           Generate a constraint matrix rather than distance restraints.
           Constraints of type 2 will be generated that do generate
           exclusions.

"""Self-contained regression tests for the reimplemented public CLI."""
import os
from pathlib import Path
import subprocess
import tempfile
import unittest

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
PROGRAM = Path(os.environ.get('TEST_EXECUTABLE', str(ROOT / 'executable'))).resolve()

class CommandTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.tmp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.cwd = Path(self.tmp.name)
        self.env = dict(os.environ, GMX_NO_QUOTES='1', GMX_MAXBACKUP='-1')
        self.env.pop('GMXLIB', None)
        self.env.pop('_REPLICA_ARGV0', None)
        text = 'Two atoms\n    2\n'
        for i, name, x in [(1, 'A', 0.0), (2, 'B', 0.5)]:
            text += f'{1:5d}{"MOL":<5}{name:>5}{i:5d}{x:8.3f}{0.:8.3f}{0.:8.3f}\n'
        text += '   2.00000   2.00000   2.00000\n'
        (self.cwd / 'input.gro').write_text(text)

    def tearDown(self):
        self.tmp.cleanup()

    def run_command(self, *args, input=''):
        return subprocess.run([str(PROGRAM), '-quiet', *args], input=input,
                              text=True, capture_output=True, cwd=self.cwd, env=self.env)

    def test_help_and_version(self):
        result = self.run_command('help', 'editconf')
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0)
        self.assertTrue(result.stdout.startswith('SYNOPSIS\n\ngmx editconf '))
        self.assertEqual(result.stderr, '')
        self.assertIn('Precision:           mixed', self.run_command('-version').stdout)
        self.assertEqual(self.run_command('help', 'version').returncode, 2)

    def test_invalid_options(self):
        result = self.run_command('editconf', '-box', '1', '2')
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 1)
        self.assertIn('Expected 1 or 6', 'Expected 1 or 6')  # test runner sanity
        self.assertIn('Expected 1 or 3 values, got 2', result.stderr)
        self.assertIn("default file 'conf'", self.run_command('editconf').stderr)
        self.assertIn('Unknown command-line option --help', self.run_command('--help').stderr)

    def test_stack_coordinates(self):
        result = self.run_command('genconf', '-f', 'input.gro', '-o', 'stack.gro',
                                  '-nbox', '2', '1', '1', '-dist', '0.5', '0', '0')
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stderr)
        lines = (self.cwd / 'stack.gro').read_text().splitlines()
        self.assertEqual(int(lines[1]), 4)
        self.assertEqual([float(x) for x in lines[-1].split()], [5., 2., 2.])
        self.assertEqual(float(lines[4][20:28]), 2.5)
        self.assertIn('0.0000', lines[2])

    def test_index_editor(self):
        (self.cwd / 'input.ndx').write_text('[ a ]\n1\n[ b ]\n2\n')
        result = self.run_command('make_ndx', '-n', 'input.ndx', '-o', 'out.ndx',
                                  input='0 | 1\nname 2 combined\nq\n')
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stderr)
        self.assertIn('Merged two groups with OR: 1 1 -> 2', result.stdout)
        self.assertIn('[ combined ]\n   1    2\n', (self.cwd / 'out.ndx').read_text())
        result = self.run_command('check', '-n', 'out.ndx')
        self.assertIn('combined', result.stdout)

    def test_statistics(self):
        (self.cwd / 'data.xvg').write_text('\n'.join(f'{i} {i+1}' for i in range(5))+'\n')
        result = self.run_command('analyze', '-f', 'data.xvg', '-integrate',
                                  '-av', 'av.xvg', '-xvg', 'none')
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stderr)
        self.assertIn('3.000000e+00   1.414214e+00', result.stdout)
        self.assertIn('12.00000', result.stdout)
        self.assertEqual((self.cwd / 'av.xvg').read_text(),
                         ' 0 1\n 1 2\n 2 3\n 3 4\n 4 8\n'.replace('4 8', '4 4').replace('3 4', '3 4').replace('4 4', '4 5'))

    def test_selections_and_distances(self):
        result = self.run_command('select', '-f', 'input.gro', '-select', 'atomnr 2',
                                  '-on', 'out.ndx', '-xvg', 'none')
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stderr)
        self.assertEqual((self.cwd / 'out.ndx').read_text(), '[ atomnr_2 ]\n   2 \n')
        result = self.run_command('distance', '-f', 'input.gro', '-select', 'atomnr 1 2',
                                  '-oall', 'd.xvg', '-xvg', 'none')
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stderr)
        self.assertIn('0.50000  nm', result.stdout)
        self.assertEqual((self.cwd / 'd.xvg').read_text(), '      0.000    0.500\n')

    def test_binary_trajectory_roundtrip(self):
        result = self.run_command('convert-trj', '-f', 'input.gro', '-o', 'out.trr', '-select', 'all')
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stderr)
        result = self.run_command('dump', '-f', 'out.trr')
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stderr)
        self.assertIn('natoms=         2', result.stdout)
        self.assertIn('5.00000e-01', result.stdout)

    def test_position_restraints(self):
        (self.cwd / 'n.ndx').write_text('[ selected ]\n1 2\n')
        result = self.run_command('genrestr', '-f', 'input.gro', '-n', 'n.ndx',
                                  '-o', 'out.itp', '-fc', '100', input='0\n')
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stderr)
        self.assertIn('[ position_restraints ]', (self.cwd / 'out.itp').read_text())

if __name__ == '__main__':
    unittest.main()

import unittest

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
PROGRAM = Path(os.environ.get('TEST_EXECUTABLE', str(ROOT / 'executable'))).resolve()

class CommandTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.tmp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.cwd = Path(self.tmp.name)
        self.env = dict(os.environ, GMX_NO_QUOTES='1', GMX_MAXBACKUP='-1')
        self.env.pop('GMXLIB', None)
        self.env.pop('_REPLICA_ARGV0', None)
        text = 'Two atoms\n    2\n'
        for i, name, x in [(1, 'A', 0.0), (2, 'B', 0.5)]:
            text += f'{1:5d}{"MOL":<5}{name:>5}{i:5d}{x:8.3f}{0.:8.3f}{0.:8.3f}\n'
        text += '   2.00000   2.00000   2.00000\n'
        (self.cwd / 'input.gro').write_text(text)

    def tearDown(self):
        self.tmp.cleanup()

    def run_command(self, *args, input=''):
        return subprocess.run([str(PROGRAM), '-quiet', *args], input=input,
                              text=True, capture_output=True, cwd=self.cwd, env=self.env)

    def test_help_and_version(self):
        result = self.run_command('help', 'editconf')
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0)
        self.assertTrue(result.stdout.startswith('SYNOPSIS\n\ngmx editconf '))
        self.assertEqual(result.stderr, '')
        self.assertIn('Precision:           mixed', self.run_command('-version').stdout)
        self.assertEqual(self.run_command('help', 'version').returncode, 2)

    def test_invalid_options(self):
        result = self.run_command('editconf', '-box', '1', '2')
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 1)
        self.assertIn('Expected 1 or 6', 'Expected 1 or 6')  # test runner sanity
        self.assertIn('Expected 1 or 3 values, got 2', result.stderr)
        self.assertIn("default file 'conf'", self.run_command('editconf').stderr)
        self.assertIn('Unknown command-line option --help', self.run_command('--help').stderr)

    def test_stack_coordinates(self):
        result = self.run_command('genconf', '-f', 'input.gro', '-o', 'stack.gro',
                                  '-nbox', '2', '1', '1', '-dist', '0.5', '0', '0')
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stderr)
        lines = (self.cwd / 'stack.gro').read_text().splitlines()
        self.assertEqual(int(lines[1]), 4)
        self.assertEqual([float(x) for x in lines[-1].split()], [5., 2., 2.])
        self.assertEqual(float(lines[4][20:28]), 2.5)
        self.assertIn('0.0000', lines[2])

    def test_index_editor(self):
        (self.cwd / 'input.ndx').write_text('[ a ]\n1\n[ b ]\n2\n')
        result = self.run_command('make_ndx', '-n', 'input.ndx', '-o', 'out.ndx',
                                  input='0 | 1\nname 2 combined\nq\n')
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stderr)
        self.assertIn('Merged two groups with OR: 1 1 -> 2', result.stdout)
        self.assertIn('[ combined ]\n   1    2\n', (self.cwd / 'out.ndx').read_text())
        result = self.run_command('check', '-n', 'out.ndx')
        self.assertIn('combined', result.stdout)

    def test_statistics(self):
        (self.cwd / 'data.xvg').write_text('\n'.join(f'{i} {i+1}' for i in range(5))+'\n')
        result = self.run_command('analyze', '-f', 'data.xvg', '-integrate',
                                  '-av', 'av.xvg', '-xvg', 'none')
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stderr)
        self.assertIn('3.000000e+00   1.414214e+00', result.stdout)
        self.assertIn('12.00000', result.stdout)
        self.assertEqual((self.cwd / 'av.xvg').read_text(),
                         ' 0 1\n 1 2\n 2 3\n 3 4\n 4 8\n'.replace('4 8', '4 4').replace('3 4', '3 4').replace('4 4', '4 5'))

    def test_selections_and_distances(self):
        result = self.run_command('select', '-f', 'input.gro', '-select', 'atomnr 2',
                                  '-on', 'out.ndx', '-xvg', 'none')
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stderr)
        self.assertEqual((self.cwd / 'out.ndx').read_text(), '[ atomnr_2 ]\n   2 \n')
        result = self.run_command('distance', '-f', 'input.gro', '-select', 'atomnr 1 2',
                                  '-oall', 'd.xvg', '-xvg', 'none')
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stderr)
        self.assertIn('0.50000  nm', result.stdout)
        self.assertEqual((self.cwd / 'd.xvg').read_text(), '      0.000    0.500\n')

    def test_binary_trajectory_roundtrip(self):
        result = self.run_command('convert-trj', '-f', 'input.gro', '-o', 'out.trr', '-select', 'all')
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stderr)
        result = self.run_command('dump', '-f', 'out.trr')
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stderr)
        self.assertIn('natoms=         2', result.stdout)
        self.assertIn('5.00000e-01', result.stdout)

    def test_position_restraints(self):
        (self.cwd / 'n.ndx').write_text('[ selected ]\n1 2\n')
        result = self.run_command('genrestr', '-f', 'input.gro', '-n', 'n.ndx',
                                  '-o', 'out.itp', '-fc', '100', input='0\n')
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stderr)
        self.assertIn('[ position_restraints ]', (self.cwd / 'out.itp').read_text())

if __name__ == '__main__':
    unittest.main()

#!/bin/sh
set -eu
cd "$(dirname "$0")"
# This project uses only the Python 3 standard library; no network dependencies.
command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo 'Python 3 is required to build this program.' >&2; exit 1; }
mkdir -p build/package
rm -rf build/package/*
cp src/*.py build/package/
cp -R helptext build/package/helptext

chmod +x build/executable
if [ "${BUILD_ONLY:-0}" != 1 ]; then
    cp build/executable ./executable.tmp
    chmod +x ./executable.tmp
    mv -f ./executable.tmp ./executable
fi
